It is boilerplate and circular. Delete the clause. • Definition of the estimator class T_n (synth_6): the same 28-label 'in the setting of \cref{...}' clause ends the definition. Delete it. • Introduction, stand-alone paragraph 'The statistical results hold under the stated model and sampling assumptions.' asserts nothing. Delete. • Formalization jargon 'handle': 'Normalized paired prior construction ... The paired-prior handle consists of'. Rename to 'paired-prior construction'. • Formalization jargon 'certificate': 'risk certificate' (introduction), 'second-moment certificate' (Appendix A opening and after the interval lemma), '\textbf{(Uniform risk certificate.)} C_U>0 certifies', 'uniform estimation certificate'. Replace with 'uniform risk bound'. • Verification note jargon: 'frozen statistical assumptions', 'theorem-local verification disclosures retain the precise scope'. Rewrite in plain terms and state explicitly whether any displayed result depends on an unformalized cited input. • Lean artifact in the baseline-coordinates definition: 'The collection of all such atoms is finite and has decidable equality.' Delete 'and has decidable equality'. • Empty-alphabet d=0 conventions are repeated in the definitions of potential coordinates, full-data atoms, observed records, the full-data law, the identifying functional and the identification lemma ('where the baseline domain is empty when d=0'; 'the assertion for that case is vacuous'), although the analysis uses d>=1. Take d>=1 throughout and delete them. • Honest interval class definition: 'for nonnegative integers n,d and real parameters q,alpha' conflicts with n,d>=1, q in [1/2,1], alpha in (0,1/2) used everywhere else. State the actual ranges. • Wrong cross-reference in the interval-class definition: 'tau(P) is the treatment-effect functional in \cref{obj:def:identified-functional}'. That definition defines Psi(P_O); tau(P) is defined only in running prose. Give tau(P) its own definition environment and cite it. • Central target tau(P) and the observation map / P_O are defined only in running prose, while trivial coordinate spaces get numbered definitions. Promote them to definition environments. • Near-duplicate definitions: mu_P(x,a,s) is defined in synth_5 and again inside the identifying-functional definition, where it is written with subscript P although Psi is a function of P_O. Define it once and cite it. • Near-duplicate definitions synth_3, synth_4, synth_2, synth_1 (potential coordinates, full-data atom, observed record, full-data law) should be merged into one 'data structure' definition. The full-data law definition merely restates the atom definition. • The observed-record definition uses O for both the space and a record: 'The observed-record space O consists of tuples O=(X,A,S,R,RY)\in...'. Use distinct symbols (e.g. \mathcal O for the space). • Unused notation in Setup: '\|f\|_{p,Q}=(\mathbb E_Q|f|^p)^{1/p}', 'u\lesssim v' and 'u\asymp v' are defined but never used. Delete them or use them. • Duplicate symbols for log(e+n): \ell_n in the main text and upper-bound proof, L in the paired-prior definition and converse proof, where L(o) is also the lower interval endpoint. Use \ell_n throughout. • Symbol clash on m: 'm=n/8' in the estimator and 'm=K-1' in the prior construction. Rename one. • Symbol clash on h: 'h=K^{-2}' in the prior construction and the radius 'h_{n,d,q,alpha}'. Rename one. • Symbol clash on c_0: 'c_0=1/16' in the prior construction and the universal constant 'c_0' in the parametric-floor and prior-reduction lemmas. Rename one. • Symbol clash on a: the algorithm writes 'a_j=a' (treatment arm of cell j) and 'a_v' (polynomial coefficients) in the same environment. The proofs also use a_risk, a_len, a_pt. Rename the coefficients. • Coefficients a_v are never defined explicitly: '1-Q_k(z)=\sum_{v=1}^{k-1}a_vz^v' is used as an implicit definition. Say 'where a_v denote the coefficients of the polynomial 1-Q_k'. • Symbol clash on T: Chebyshev T_k, estimators T in \mathcal T_n, and the tail event \mathcal T_P in the interval proof. Rename the tail event and consider another letter for generic estimators. • Symbol clash on delta: 'delta=1-q' and the Dirac masses '\Pi_-^{small}=\delta_{P_{-,small}}' in the converse proof. • Symbol clash on B, U, C, mu: threshold 'B=256\ell_n' against the event 'B\subseteq O^n' in the TV display; count U_j against endpoint U(o); counts C_j, C'_j against constants C, C_U; '\mu_{obs}=P_O^{\otimes n}' (a measure) against \mu_P, \mu_0 (means). Rename. • Projection Pi_{[-1,1]}, the Chebyshev convention T_k(cos theta)=cos(k theta) and the falling-factorial convention are each stated in the paragraph before the algorithm and again inside it; the projection is stated again in the proposition. State each once. • Complete-arrival proposition contains a vacuous display: 'g_{n,d,1}=(1-1)\min\{1,d/(n\log(e+n))\}=0'. It also re-defines Pi, Y_i^{obs} and tau(P) inside the statement. Trim to the substantive claims. • 'the supplied fifth coordinate' (algorithm step 1, the proposition, 'Completion of the main comparisons') is formalization phrasing. Write 'the observed outcome mark RY'. • Interval definition: 'C_U is any universal constant for which the upper squared-risk bound ... holds' leaves the procedure not uniquely defined. Fix C_U as the explicit constant from the upper-risk lemma and cite it. • Honest-interval lemma takes as a hypothesis ('Uniform risk certificate') exactly the conclusion of the upper-risk lemma, with the odd phrase 'under any iid observed-sample law'. Cite the lemma instead of restating it. • Prior-reduction lemma statement restates the parametric floors of the previous lemma ('Throughout the stated parameter range, the parametric bounds are ...') and declares 'Let c_beta denote the fixed separation constant selected from the normalized converse' without a \cref. Remove the restatement and add the \cref. • Normalized-converse theorem: 'supported on \mathcal M(d,q) ..., whose laws satisfy \cref{obj:ass:randomized-independence,...}' is redundant with membership in the class. Delete the second clause. • Proof of the point-risk theorem, step 4: 'we use the conditional real supremum: ... a set unbounded above is assigned supremum zero', followed by a case split on unbounded risks. This is a proof-assistant convention, and the case is impossible since the risks lie in [0,4]. Delete and note boundedness. The same artifact is in the interval-theorem proof, step 5 ('For an unbounded-above collection, the real-valued supremum is assigned the value zero'). • Proof of the point-risk theorem, step 2: 'Apply \cref{obj:lem:prior-reduction} with alpha=1/4' is an arbitrary instantiation artifact. Restate the lemma so the point-risk bound does not require choosing alpha. • The range argument for the estimator (Poisson weights omega_N, stream averages) appears twice nearly verbatim: step 3 of the honest-interval lemma proof and step 3 of the point-risk theorem proof. State it once as a lemma or remark. • Nonemptiness of M(d,q) via the filler law is proved three times (point-risk proof step 4, interval proof step 3, proposition proof step 2), though the parametric-floor proof already exhibits members. State it once. • Appendix C is titled 'Testing reductions and proofs of the main results' but contains only a narrative 'Completion of the main comparisons'; the proofs are in the later appendix 'Proofs of the main results'. Retitle Appendix C and merge or cross-reference the 'Completion' subsection. • Redundant heading '\section*{Appendices}' immediately after \appendix. Delete. • The introduction's Kallus-Mao sentence ('The closest identification and efficiency benchmark is \citet[Lemma~1.1 ...') and the first sentence of Related work are near-verbatim duplicates. Shorten the introduction's version. • The model-enlargement paragraph appears twice nearly verbatim: last paragraph of 'Statistical implications' and third paragraph of 'Limitations and future work' ('Any law class on the same observed experiment, with the same treatment-effect target, that contains the submodels ... inherits'). Keep one. • Citations without locators, contrary to the paper's own convention: \citet{CausalSmith2026,CausalSmith2026Annotation} (three places), \citet{Armstrong2021}, \citep{WuYang2016,Wu2020} and \citet{Wu2020} in Appendix B, \citep{vanDerVaart1998}, \citep{ImbensRubin2015}, and \citep{KallusMao2025} after the consistency, MAR and arrival-floor assumptions. Add section or theorem locators. • Inconsistent citation markup: the identification formula is cited as '\href{https://academic.oup.com/...}{\citet[Lemma~1.1, equation~(10), ...]{KallusMao2025}}'. Drop the \href wrapper. • Abstract term 'A polynomial-and-ratio correction weighted by missing-outcome cell membership' is unglossed at first use. Add a brief plain-word description or simplify. • The estimator class \mathcal T_n depends on d but the notation suppresses it. Write \mathcal T_{n,d} or note the dependence. • Proof displays write the random sample as lower-case o inside expectations ('\mathbb E_P[\{T(o)-\tau(P)\}^2]', point-risk proof step 4), against O^n elsewhere. Use O^n. • Algorithm step 1 sets 'k=\max\{1,\lfloor\ell_n/64\rfloor\}' although k is used only in the branch \ell_n>=128, where the max is inactive. Steps 2-5 are computed even in branches that discard them. State the branch selection first and define the tuning parameters only for the conditional-average branch. • Uninformative sentences: after the main theorems, 'Together, these arguments give the matching comparisons in ...'; in Appendix A, 'Each of these choices is part of \cref{obj:def:mm-estimator}'; in Setup, 'The cellwise arrival probability ... are therefore defined for every cell.' Delete. • Introduction: 'The statistical results hold under the stated model and sampling assumptions.' This clause adds no usable information. Delete it or replace it with a specific interpretation of the assumptions. • Cellwise arrival definition: 'In the setting of \cref{obj:ass:iid,...,obj:synth_6}, define...' expands into a paper-wide list of prerequisites, including results and objects defined later. Replace the list with the full-data law and relevant coordinate definitions; these conditional quantities require neither the estimator nor the minimax theorems. • Measurable estimator definition: 'in the setting of \cref{obj:ass:iid,...,obj:synth_5}' repeats another paper-wide list of forward references. Delete that trailing list and retain the observed-space reference already supplied. • Setup: 'For a nonnegative integer d' and 'the baseline domain is empty when d=0' recur across the potential-data, full-data, observed-space, law, and functional definitions despite the positive-d statistical domain. Group the empty-alphabet convention into one sentence or verification note and use the positive-d domain in the statistical exposition. • Setup: the separate definitions 'Baseline and potential coordinates,' 'Full-data atom coordinates,' 'Observed records and space,' and 'Full-data probability law' repeatedly enumerate overlapping coordinates. Group these definitions into a coordinated setup block with one coordinate table or display and a single observation map. • Honest interval definition: 'for nonnegative integers n,d and real parameters q,alpha' conflicts editorially with the positive-integer and restricted-parameter domains used to define the referenced law class and statistical criteria. State the operative domain n,d≥1, q∈[1/2,1], alpha∈(0,1/2), and move broader formal domains to the verification supplement. • Honest interval definition: 'tau(P) is the treatment-effect functional in \cref{obj:def:identified-functional}' points to an environment defining Psi rather than tau. Replace this clause with the explicit formula tau(P)=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)] or reference a dedicated target definition. • Normalized paired prior definition: 'The paired-prior handle consists of...' uses implementation terminology as a mathematical object name. Replace 'handle' with 'construction' or 'collection of priors and auxiliary experiments' in the sentence and environment title. • Normalized-prior appendix: 'The normalized priors ... and complete sample mixtures ... therefore belong to the causal model and its original sampling experiment' conflates priors, their supporting laws, and sample-mixture distributions. Rewrite: the priors are supported on the causal law class, and their mixtures are probability laws on the original observed-sample space. • Prior-reduction subsection: 'choose a positive separation constant c_beta satisfying \cref{obj:thm:normalized-converse}' is followed by the lemma's 'selected from the normalized converse' without a cross-reference. Attach \cref{obj:thm:normalized-converse} to the latter named reference. • Main estimation section: 'Let C_U be a universal upper-risk constant' introduces a statistical bound clearly, but the subsequent 'risk certificate' terminology recurs throughout the paper. Replace reader-facing 'risk certificate,' 'uniform risk certificate,' and 'certifies' with 'uniform risk bound,' 'upper-risk constant,' and 'satisfies' respectively, including the interval lemma's hypothesis heading. • Upper-risk appendix: 'the second-moment certificate used to construct honest confidence intervals' and 'the risk certificate for \cref{obj:lem:honest-interval-construction}' repeat verification terminology in statistical exposition. Replace both with 'second-moment bound' or 'uniform squared-error bound.' • Limitations: 'a procedure that selects its degree of correction or interval radius from the data' follows a claim that the construction uses the floor, although its displayed degree k depends on n. Separate adaptation of the interval radius to an unknown floor from alternative tuning of the correction degree; identify precisely where q enters the displayed estimator. • Algorithm: Steps 2–5 describe a randomized construction even when Step 6 selects a direct branch, and Step 2 says 'perform the following three steps' while the overall enumeration subsequently continues. State the output branches first and nest the randomized construction entirely inside the conditional-average branch, with explicit substep numbering. • Algorithm exposition: the Chebyshev convention, falling-factorial convention, and projection formula appear immediately before the algorithm and then again inside it. Keep one definition of each and remove the duplicate displays. • Post-upper-risk exposition: p_j, b_j, theta_j, and lambda_j rename the proof's pi_j, w_j, eta_j, and zeta_j for the same quantities. Reuse one set of symbols to avoid an unnecessary second notation system. • Paired-prior definition: m=K-1 reuses the estimator's m=n/8 for an unrelated polynomial degree parameter. Rename the interpolation degree, for example k_int, and update its uses in nodes, products, and interpolation identities. • Paired-prior definition: c_0=1/16 reuses the symbol later assigned to the parametric risk-floor constant. Rename the prior perturbation amplitude, for example c_pair, and preserve c_0 for the sampling floor. • Proof of the point frontier: 'a set unbounded above is assigned supremum zero' imports a conditional-real-supremum convention into standard statistical prose. Replace the entire unbounded-case discussion with the already available fact that every admissible squared-error risk lies in [0,4], so ordinary finite suprema apply. • Proof of the interval frontier: 'For an unbounded-above collection, the real-valued supremum is assigned the value zero' is likewise unnecessary and misleading for lengths bounded by two. Replace this discussion with the endpoint bound 0≤U-L≤2 and use the ordinary supremum. • Proofs of the honest interval lemma and point frontier independently expand the same Poisson-weight and stream-assignment argument establishing the estimator's range. State measurability and range once after the estimator construction and reference that result in subsequent proofs. • Proof of the honest interval lemma: the full atomwise expansion beginning 'Define W_P=supp(P)' proves the elementary bound tau(P)∈[-1,1] already stated in Setup. Replace it with the binary-potential-outcome bound and its expectation. • Parametric-floor proof: 'If the error probability under the first law is at most that under the second...' splits a maximum-risk argument into redundant cases. Replace both cases with the single maximum-error-probability inequality. • Main-comparison and prior-reduction proofs repeatedly display 'sqrt(n)>0,' '(sqrt(n))^2=n,' and positivity of each minimum entry. Compress these elementary checks into the comparison inequalities they justify. • Complete-arrival proposition: the samplewise projection inequality, worst-law inequality, estimator identity, and endpoint rate are restated at length in its proof and in surrounding commentary. Retain the substantive proposition and shorten the commentary to its randomized-trial interpretation. • Appendix organization: 'Completion of the main comparisons' summarizes proofs that appear again after 'Verification note' under 'Proofs of the main results.' Place the main proofs directly after the testing reductions and remove the duplicate completion subsection. • Upper-risk appendix: the paragraphs after the proof repeat the estimator's stream roles, projection, averaging, and complete list of branch conditions already described in the main section. Replace these paragraphs with a short explanation of the two controlling quantities: missing-cell mass and arrived-count intensity. • Introduction and Related work repeat substantially the same citation sequence and contribution sentence. Keep a short positioning paragraph in the Introduction and reserve detailed conditions and locators for Related work. • Verification note: 'The theorem-local verification disclosures retain the precise scope of each result' refers to disclosures that are not present in the supplied manuscript. Supply those disclosures or replace the sentence with an accurate description of the verification information actually included. • Author footnote: 'as recorded in the verification appendix (scope, toolchain, commit, and any statement conditional on a published input)' promises toolchain and commit information absent from the displayed Verification note. Add the exact toolchain and commit identifiers and identify any published-input dependencies. • Author footnote: 'Each displayed formal statement is either mapped to a Lean declaration or marked as a presentation-level definition' promises a mapping or marking that the supplied text does not show. Add the statement-to-declaration mapping and explicit presentation-level markings in the verification appendix.
